children: Blockchain education platform EasyA is planning to go public.
EasyA on Friday said it has confidentially filed a draft registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed direct stock listing.

The London company, which previously said it planned to become a publicly-traded company during 2027, said the direct listing would take place after the SEC completes its review process, subject to market conditions.

Direct listings differ from traditional initial public offerings in that companies take their shares to the stock market directly without issuing new shares, saving money that in a more traditional IPO would be shelled out to investment banks.
The SEC's confidential filing process lets regulators and companies engage in a back-and-forth dialogue about disclosures as they wrap up the paperwork.
EasyA earlier this month said its app has more than 1 million users and partners with more than 350 of the world's top academic institutions, adding that its ecosystem is worth nearly $30 billion.
